doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Kid Punch Miller and the pawn-shop horn
summary: Pops on Punch Miller imitating Louis, and the pawn-shop horn near-chopping story.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I think Louis and Joe started that round there, because they played all them big numbers like Snaggit and- Yeah, they played the duets. Yeah. And one trumpet they wanted to play, they wanted to be outstanding by themselves. They had a guy they called Kid Punch. We saw him in New Orleans. Well everything he wanted to play, he wanted to make his endings like Louis. Oh, he's got power if he just knows his horn. He's still playing? He's got power if he just knows his horn. Sounds like power.
Oh yeah, we saw a punch coming. He's got the power. But he don't know his horn. You don't know him, huh? No. You know Guy Kelly? He sounds like- You remember Guy Kelly?

Yeah. Well look, if you see him, you see Guy Kelly, you see him. Look just like him for the world. Guy Kelly worked for him, brother. Yeah, I bought, I had to buy it at what it mean to Lorenzo Stoyle, bought, paid three dollars for a horn out of the pawn shop for a- We couldn't punch, he didn't have no horn. Then he made us mad, we were going to take the horn, but Jack Carey, much Carey's brother, stopped him from taking the horn. I had the hatchet to chop the horn in half. I was going to give Stoyle's his half and I was going to take the other half. You know, he was going to cut it right there. I was going to tell you, no, give me my half and I wasn't going to hatch it, man. Let me do some crazy things, man.
